finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a malicious file name that includes shell metacharacters or commands.
finding.assumptions: The program does not sanitize or validate the file name input before using it in file operations.

parsed.change_summary: Added sanitization to remove spaces and subsequent characters from the file name input to prevent OS command injection.
parsed.how_trigger_is_blocked: The trigger is blocked by sanitizing the file name input to remove any spaces and subsequent characters. This prevents the attacker from injecting shell metacharacters or commands into the file name.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1) Reviewed the code to identify any operation that could execute a shell command using the user‑supplied file name. The only sink is policeStationFile.open(fileName), which simply opens a file descriptor; it does not invoke a shell or any system call that interprets the string as a command. 2) Confirmed that no subsequent code uses system(), exec*, popen(), or similar functions with the file name. 3) Checked that the file name is read from std::cin and passed directly to std::ifstream::open, which is safe from command injection. 4) Considered potential path‑traversal or other file‑access issues, but these are unrelated to OS command injection.

findings.title: Directory Traversal
findings.trigger: An attacker can provide a file name that includes directory traversal sequences (e.g., '../') to access files outside the intended directory.
findings.assumptions: The program does not sanitize or validate the file name input before using it in file operations.

findings.title: File Overwrite
findings.trigger: An attacker can provide a file name that points to an existing file, causing it to be overwritten without any warning or confirmation.
findings.assumptions: The program does not check if the file already exists before opening it in write mode.

findings.title: Resource Exhaustion
findings.trigger: An attacker can provide a large number of invalid file names, causing the program to repeatedly prompt the user and consume system resources.
findings.assumptions: The program does not limit the number of times it prompts the user for a valid file name.
